title: In this world, every lie you've ever told floats above your head.
formula: Rule -> you're the exception -> everyday fallout x3 -> snap -> deadpan double -> rule's own logic -> callback loop
facts: Fiction: no sources needed. Rule: a glowing number above each person's head counts every lie they have ever told, and goes up the moment they lie.

lines.narration: In this world, every lie you've ever told floats above your head as a number. Yours says *4,000*.
lines.scene: Cold open: busy street, everyone has small glowing numbers; yours is a huge flashing 4,000 and a pigeon is staring at it.
lines.spoken: In this world, every lie you've ever told floats above your head as a number. Yours says four thousand.

lines.narration: Most people are around 40, your grandma's at 2, and the baby next door is already at *11*.
lines.scene: Quick inserts: average person '40', sweet grandma '2', a smug baby '11'.
lines.camera: Hard cuts, each with a creep-in
lines.spoken: Most people are around forty, your grandma's at two, and the baby next door is already at eleven.

lines.scene: Flashback card: tiny you blaming a broken vase on the cat; your counter ticks up.

lines.narration: Job interview. 'What's your biggest weakness?' You say you work too hard. 4,000 and *1*.
lines.scene: Office. Your counter ticks 4,000 -> 4,001 with a 'ding'. The interviewer looks up at it.
lines.gag: The ding is as loud as a church bell
lines.spoken: Job interview. 'What's your biggest weakness?' You say you work too hard. [pause] Four thousand and one.

lines.narration: The interviewer just quietly writes 'no' on a sticky *note*.
lines.scene: Close-up: sticky note 'NO', placed on your forehead.

lines.narration: First date, she looks at your number, she looks at you, and she orders the most expensive thing on the *menu*.
lines.scene: Candle-lit restaurant; she glances up, then down, then points at the giant lobster on the menu.
lines.gag: The lobster arrives on a cart, enormous

lines.narration: Your mom knits you a sweater with your face on it. Upside down. You say you love it. 4,000 and *2*.
lines.scene: Living room; mom proud; sweater with your upside-down face; counter dings.
lines.spoken: Your mom knits you a sweater with your face on it, upside down. You say you love it. [sighs] Four thousand and two.

lines.narration: Then you meet someone whose number is a perfect *zero*.
lines.scene: Golden evening at a gig venue; she steps into a spotlight; '0' above her like a halo.

lines.narration: And she asks the question you've been dreading. 'So... do you like my *band*?'
lines.scene: Behind her, a band poster: four stickmen with kazoos.

lines.narration: Luckily, you're the most experienced liar on the *planet*.
lines.scene: Montage card: you on a podium with a gold medal labeled 'LYING'.
Back to her; she's looking up at your 4,002.
lines.camera: Hold with creep-in on her eyes

lines.narration: Wait... the number only goes up when you *lie*.
Every lie you know is begging you to say 'I love it'. All 4,002 of them are *chanting*.
lines.scene: Tiny ghost versions of your past lies swirl around your head, all holding 'SAY IT' signs.
lines.spoken: Every lie you know is begging you to say 'I love it'. All four thousand and two of them are chanting.

lines.narration: So for the first time in your life, you tell the truth. 'Your band is *terrible*.'
lines.scene: You, calm and sincere. Silence. A cricket card in the corner.

lines.narration: The number doesn't move. Neither does her *face*.
lines.scene: Extreme close-up on 4,002. It flickers... and stays.

lines.narration: She stares at it for a long time. Then she says it's the most romantic thing anyone has ever *said* to her.
lines.scene: She grabs your hands; tiny heart cards pop between you.

lines.narration: 50 years later, your number still says 4,002. Hers says *1*.
lines.scene: Old you and old her on a porch, matching kazoos. Counters '4,002' and '1'.
lines.gag: Your 4,002 has a cobweb on it
lines.spoken: Fifty years later, your number still says four thousand and two. [pause] Hers says one.

lines.scene: She smiles at camera. You look up at her '1', suspicious.
lines.camera: Push-in on her smile, end on the word
